done.why: I worked through the part that felt like the heart of it: the dam, the reservoir, the boat, the river and the falls. Then I drove the boat over Aragain Falls and died. The boat didn't come back after that, so I couldn't go on the river again. I walked back, closed the sluice gates to see what the water would do, and stopped there.

about: It's the old white house and the empire under it, with the most life given to Flood Control Dam #3 and the Frigid River. The place feels left behind: a dam nobody thanks, a reservoir you can drain to mud, a river hurrying toward its own end. And somebody tidy keeps going around after you, stacking fallen rock into neat heaps and putting the lamp back in the living room.

ending.what: No real ending. I died going over Aragain Falls in the magic boat at turn 122 and came back in the forest with my things scattered. The boat seemed to be gone for good, so the river was closed to me after that.

moments.note: The sword 'has plainly been in worse places than a living room.' This told me early that the descriptions had been rewritten with care.
The cave-ins in the Round Room: someone has sorted the rubble into neat heaps, 'the way some people tidy a room they have no intention of using.'
I typed 'south' and it echoed back 'South south ...'. Only then did I see that 'east' from the Round Room had taken me into the Loud Room. The map wasn't where I expected.
Water pouring over the top of the dam, a reservoir 'very full' that 'goes over it'. That's not how I remembered this place.
The dam holds back the water 'with the air of something that has been asked to do this for a very long time and has not been thanked.'
The green bubble has 'the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.'
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' I liked it once. By the third time it came back word for word it was nagging.
The river is 'going downstream as if it had heard something about the end of it and wanted to see for itself.' It's a lovely line, and it also warned me about the falls.
The boat is 'unreasonably cheerful' and 'would not care for anything sharp.' I took the hint and left the sword on the bank.
The pile said its instructions 'go on round the back', but 'read instructions' and 'turn pile over' both got 'You can't see any such thing.'
The emerald was put in a buoy and left in a river, 'which tells you something about somebody.'

'Go upstream' wasn't understood, and that wasted turn sent me over the falls. The death text was new: my plain things strewn around the fields, the valuables rolled under the house, and 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back.' It connected back to the tidy rubble.
The Gallery still describes 'a painting of unparalleled beauty', but 'examine painting' and 'take painting' both say it isn't there.
The drained reservoir: 'a stream wandering across it, looking sheepish.'
The mud 'would like to keep your boots.'
With the gates just closed and the reservoir 'low', the dam seen from below still has water spilling over the top. I couldn't tell if that was right.

wished: I wished I could read the boat instructions on the back of the folded pile before inflating it, since the text invited me to.
I wished I could look at the painting in the Gallery, since the room still describes it.
I wished I could paddle upstream or steer away from the falls. A plainer warning or one more chance before the drop would have helped.
I wished the boat came back after I died, so I could finish the river and get to the west-shore beaches.
I wished the river and the dam seen from below changed more once the gates were shut, so the water felt like one connected system.

lines.line: holding back the reservoir to the west with the air of something that has been asked to do this for a very long time and has not been thanked.
lines.why: It gives the dam a tired, unthanked dignity in a single clause. It's the best writing in the place.

lines.line: The Frigid River is wide and grey and very cold, and in a hurry, going downstream as if it had heard something about the end of it and wanted to see for itself.
lines.why: Funny and ominous together, and it quietly warns you about the falls.

lines.line: somebody has sorted the nearest of it into neat heaps, smallest nearest, the way some people tidy a room they have no intention of using.
lines.why: A small human mystery set in the rubble. It came back later in the death text.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: It made dying feel like part of the world instead of a reset, and it brought back the tidy stranger.

lines.line: Somebody put it in a buoy and left it in a river, which tells you something about somebody.
lines.why: A dry aside that makes an object hint at a person.

lines.line: a wide expanse of mud with a stream wandering across it, looking sheepish.
lines.why: The reservoir after draining. 'Sheepish' is exactly the right word.

lines.line: It is dark, and has the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.
lines.why: It made a plastic indicator light feel alive. It's also a gentle clue.

fun.why: Draining the reservoir, inflating the boat and riding the current downstream all felt good, and the descriptions kept paying me back for looking closely. It was less fun to die on a verb the game didn't recognise, lose the boat for good, and find a painting that's described but can't be touched.

engagement.why: I wanted to examine everything because the examine text kept being good: the dam, the bubble, the river, the mud, the emerald. The tidy stranger kept me curious. My engagement dropped after the boat was lost.

difficulty.why: The dam puzzle was fair. The yellow button was 'the most worn', and the bolt's 'flats worn bright' pointed at the wrench. The boat's dislike of sharp things was a good hint. The falls punished me hard for one unrecognised verb, and the carry limit kept getting in the way.

interestingness.why: The overflowing dam, the cave-ins, the someone who tidies and the rewritten death made a familiar place feel strange and lived in. I'd have liked the water to hang together more from one place to the next.

prose.why: The new descriptions are excellent: precise, dry, warm, with a running wit that gives objects some dignity and feeling. The writing is the main reason I'd come back. Small marks against it: the load-limit quip repeats word for word, and a few room texts (the Gallery painting, the dam seen from below) don't match what's actually there.
